templates.label: 记叙文
templates.desc: 记人记事：概述→经过→感悟分析
templates.steps:
要求考生写一篇记叙文，描述事件发生的时间、地点、原因、人物及结果，最后对事件进行简单分析，如：2003年6月四级作文、2003年9月四级作文、2004年6月六级作文。对这类题型，通常分为三个步骤来写：
 第一段、总结描述
 交代清楚故事涉及的人物、时间、地点：
 主题句
 第二段、具体描述
 具体描述事件发生的原因、经过和结果
 起因＋经过＋结果
 第三段、对事件的分析
 分析句1+分析句2+分析3

templates.sampleEssay:
It was about nine o'clock one evening in May. My roommate Li Ming was lying in bed, trembling with cold and coughing persistently. His head was aching so intensely that he kept groaning, and his forehead felt burning hot. We took his temperature—it was 38.5℃.

Without hesitation, I dialed "120." It wasn't long before an ambulance arrived. One roommate hurriedly brought him a blanket; another carefully supported him as he walked to the ambulance; our teacher insisted on giving him some money for medical expenses.

Was he a suspected SARS patient? Who could tell? But we didn’t retreat. When the fierce SARS epidemic was spreading, people showed fearless courage, regardless of dangers to their own health. This kind of care among individuals is genuine, selfless, and priceless devotion—or even sacrifice. And it is precisely because of such care that we can have warm families, a happy life, and a beautiful world.

templates.sampleEssay:
China finally succeeded in joining the WTO after many years' efforts. This event will influence the economy in China greatly.

Joining the WTO brings China many benefits and opportunities. As a member country, China can enjoy many rights that can boost the development of its economy. What's more, Chinese people can buy high-quality products at lower prices.

Everything has two aspects. Joining the WTO can also bring us some challenges. For example, some producers may be wiped out because of intense competition. In addition, it will be more difficult for us to get a job, as the requirements for employees will become higher.

However, this great event does more good than harm to us. What we should do is to improve ourselves to become qualified for certain positions and live a better life.

templates.label: 英文信函
templates.desc: 称呼→目的→主体→反驳→落款
templates.steps:
要求考生根据提纲写一封英文书信，如2005年12月六级作文、2005年1月四六级作文、2004年6月四六级作文、2004年1月四级作文。对这类题型，通常分为5个步骤来写：
 第一、文章开头：称呼
 第二段、寒暄语句，引出写信的目的：
 寒暄句＋主题句（注：寒暄句和主题句可以是同一个句子）
 第三段、根据提纲扩展主体段落：
 主题句＋扩展句1+扩展句2+扩展句3
 第四段、表明自己的观点，并结束书信主体段落
 在最后要他谈自己的看法
 第五段、寒暄句+落款

templates.sampleEssay:
Dear Mr. President,

This letter comes to you from one of your students. In it, some opinions are put forward for you to reflect upon.

As you know, our students are the main customers of the university canteen. Unfortunately, we do not find the service there satisfying sometimes. The food is not as nutritious as it should be; as a result, some of us become thinner and weaker during our time at university. Besides, canteen staff sometimes serve steamed buns with their bare hands—without washing them first. Moreover, the prices are somewhat higher than they ought to be.

Some people may argue that measures have been taken and improvements are underway. For instance, IC cards have replaced cash payments in the canteen, and the attitude of service staff is gradually improving. However, in my opinion, progress has been neither swift nor thorough.

To be brief, though a bit dissatisfied with the present canteen conditions, I do believe that, with the efforts of all concerned, we can solve these problems. Thank you.
sampleParagraphs: This letter comes to you from one of your students. In it, some opinions are put forward for you to reflect upon.

As you know, our students are the main customers of the university canteen. Unfortunately, we do not find the service there satisfying sometimes. The food is not as nutritious as it should be; as a result, some of us become thinner and weaker during our time at university. Besides, canteen staff sometimes serve steamed buns with their bare hands—without washing them first. Moreover, the prices are somewhat higher than they ought to be.

Some people may argue that measures have been taken and improvements are underway. For instance, IC cards have replaced cash payments in the canteen, and the attitude of service staff is gradually improving. However, in my opinion, progress has been neither swift nor thorough.
To be brief, though a bit dissatisfied with the present canteen conditions, I do believe that, with the efforts of all concerned, we can solve these problems. Thank you.

patterns26.title: ~~~ the + ~ est + 名词 + (that) + 主词 + have ever + seen ( known/heard/had/read, etc)
patterns26.pattern: ~~~ the most + 形容词 + 名词 + (that) + 主词 + have ever + seen ( known/heard/had/read, etc

examples.en: Helen is the most beautiful girl that I have ever seen.
examples.zh: 海伦是我所看过最美丽的女孩。

examples.en: Mr. Chang is the kindest teacher that I have ever had.
examples.zh: 张老师是我曾经遇到最仁慈的教师。

patterns26.title: Nothing is + ~~~ er than to + V Nothing is + more + 形容词 + than to + V

examples.en: Nothing is more important than to receive education.
examples.zh: 没有比接受教育更重要的事。

patterns26.title: ~~~ cannot emphasize the importance of ~~~ too much.（再怎么强调...的重要性也不为过。）

examples.en: We cannot emphasize the importance of protecting our eyes too much.   我们再怎么强调保护眼睛的重要性也不为过。

patterns26.title: There is no denying that + S + V ...（不可否认的...）

examples.en: There is no denying that the qualities of our living have gone from bad to worse. 不可否认的，我们的生活品质已经每况愈下。

patterns26.title: It is universally acknowledged that + 句子~~ （全世界都知道...）

examples.en: It is universally acknowledged that trees are indispensable to us.
examples.zh: 全世界都知道树木对我们是不可或缺的。

patterns26.title: There is no doubt that + 句子~~ （毫无疑问的...）

examples.en: There is no doubt that our educational system leaves something to be desired.   毫无疑问的我们的教育制度令人不满意。

patterns26.title: An advantage of ~~~ is that + 句子 （...的优点是...）

examples.en: An advantage of using the solar energy is that it won't create (produce) any pollution.   使用太阳能的优点是它不会制造任何污染。

patterns26.title: The reason why + 句子 ~~~ is that + 句子 （...的原因是...）

examples.en: The reason why we have to grow trees is that they can provide us with fresh air./ The reason why we have to grow trees is that they can supply fresh air for us. 我们必须种树的原因是它们能供应我们新鲜的空气。

patterns26.title: The + ~er + S + V, ~~~ the + ~er + S + V ~~~
patterns26.pattern: The + more + Adj + S + V, ~~~ the + more + Adj + S + V ~~~（愈...愈...）

examples.en: The harder you work, the more progress you make.
The more books we read, the more learned we become.
examples.zh: 我们书读愈多，我们愈有学问。

examples.en: 十 、By +Ving, ~~ can ~~ （借着...，..能够..）
By taking exercise, we can always stay healthy.
examples.zh: 借着做运动，我们能够始终保持健康。

patterns26.title: ~~~ enable + Object（受词）+ to + V （..使..能够..）

examples.en: Listening to music enable us to feel relaxed.
examples.zh: 听音乐使我们能够感觉轻松。

patterns26.title: It is time + S + 过去式 （该是...的时候了）

examples.en: It is time the authorities concerned took proper steps to solve the trafficproblems. 该是有关当局采取适当的措施来解决交通问题的时候了。

patterns26.title: Those who ~~~ （...的人...）

examples.en: Those who violate traffic regulations should be punished.
examples.zh: 违反交通规定的人应该受处罚。

patterns26.title: be + forced/compelled/obliged + to + V （不得不...）

examples.en: Since the examination is around the corner, I am compelled to give up doing sports. 既然考试迫在眉睫，我不得不放弃做运动。

patterns26.title: It is conceivable that + 句子 （可想而知的）
patterns26.pattern:
It is obvious that + 句子 （明显的）
It is apparent that + 句子 （显然的）

examples.en: It is conceivable that knowledge plays an important role in our life. 可想而知，知识在我们的一生中扮演一个重要的角色。

examples.en: Since he went to senior high school, he has worked very hard.自从他上高中，他一直很用功。

patterns26.title: be based on （以...为基础）

examples.en: The progress of the society is based on harmony.
examples.zh: 社会的进步是以和谐为基础的。

patterns26.title: be closely related to ~~ （与...息息相关）

examples.en: Taking exercise is closely related to health.
examples.zh: 做运动与健康息息相关。

patterns26.title: Get into the habit of + Ving

examples.en: We should get into the habit of keeping good hours.
examples.zh: 我们应该养成早睡早起的习惯。

examples.zh: 我们的交通状况令人不满意。

patterns26.title: Have a great influence on ~~~ （对...有很大的影响）

examples.en: Smoking has a great influence on our health.
examples.zh: 抽烟对我们的健康有很大的影响。

patterns26.title: do good to （对...有益），do harm to （对...有害）

examples.en: Reading does good to our mind.读书对心灵有益。
Overwork does harm to health.工作过度对健康有害。

pastExams.titleEn: Limiting the Use of Disposable Plastic Bags
pastExams.directions: Limiting the Use of Disposable Plastic Bags
pastExams.essay:
Disposable plastic bags were once widely used in China. When we went shopping at supermarkets and department stores, shop assistants often provided free plastic bags for our convenience. For a while, life without them seemed unimaginable to most of us.

However, disposable plastic bags cause severe damage to the environment. Customers usually throw them away after use, and because they are thin and difficult to decompose, these plastic products persist for hundreds of years. This poses a serious threat to our land and water resources.

Nowadays, the government has introduced regulations to limit the use of disposable plastic bags: they are no longer provided for free. In some stores, to raise public awareness of environmental protection, plastic bags are sold at a much higher price. As a result, people are changing their habits—paper bags and cloth bags, which had disappeared for a long time, are making a comeback in daily life. Indeed, by limiting their use, everyone contributes to improving the environment.

How to improve psychological health?
pastExams.essay:
As is known to all, psychological health is as important as— if not more important than—physical health for students during their growth. However, it is quite worrying that some students today are not psychologically healthy.

Undoubtedly, schools and universities should take great responsibility for students' psychological well-being. Relevant courses and activities should be introduced so that students become more aware of the importance of psychological health and learn appropriate ways to maintain and improve it. For example, a psychological counseling hotline or on-campus counseling office should be available for students seeking support.

Of course, no improvement in psychological health can be achieved without students’ own efforts. From my perspective, they should strive to stay positive and optimistic, and follow sound guidance from their schools. More specifically, they can participate in activities such as voluntary work to cultivate an open and caring mindset. Meanwhile, they should avoid harmful influences from cyberspace.

Will E-books Replace Traditional Books?

Recent decades have seen the rapid development of information technology, and E-books have thus found their way into our daily life. Because of their wide and rapid popularity, an increasing controversy has arisen over whether E-books will replace traditional books.

Many people believe that E-books will soon replace traditional books, as they offer several advantages. First, E-books are more accessible: readers need only log onto the internet to read online. Second, thanks to advanced technology, E-books cost much less, allowing readers to save money. Last but not least, reading E-books has become part of daily life—especially appealing to young users, who make up the majority of electronic product consumers.

As far as I am concerned, it is unlikely that E-books will replace traditional books for many reasons. For example, prolonged reading of E-books can harm our eyesight, and printed books remain more accessible to many readers, as computers and the internet have not yet been普及 (→ corrected to: “have not yet reached every corner of our lives”).

With the reform of Chinese higher education, more and more colleges and universities emphasize cultivating students' abilities. As a result, selective courses are available not only for top academic performers but also for students of average ability.

On the other hand, others embrace the idea of liberal education, so courses in literature, history, and philosophy are most popular.

Although my major is chemistry, the electives I attend most frequently are English literature, Introduction to Classical Music, and Different Schools of Western Painting. pastExams.essay:
The Digital Age

Living in the digital age, we are unavoidably exposed to all kinds of digital products—such as digital cameras, computers, and televisions—which are increasing in both variety and quantity. Believe it or not, look around yourself, and you can easily find one or two of these devices.

Here is a question: what kind of influence do digital products have on people’s lives? Frankly speaking, these modern digital products offer us a more convenient life than before. For example, digital cameras make it possible to delete or correct 'unsuccessful' photos—something impossible with traditional cameras. However, unfortunately, these fashionable digital items have cultivated a generation increasingly isolated from real-life interaction. It is hard to imagine that someone so accustomed to online chatting on a digital mobile phone could still be capable of effective face-to-face communication with others. Finally, excessive dependence on digital devices makes people seem more indifferent to the real world—a reality we may be reluctant to admit, yet must accept.

Thus, as a generation surrounded by all kinds of digital miracles, we might as well proactively limit our use of some of them, despite the efficiency and comfort they provide. Don’t forget those old days when you traveled a long distance by train just to visit an old school friend—a meaningful, time-consuming effort that, in today’s digital era, has been largely replaced by instant online chatting.

pastExams.essay:
Should One Expect a Reward When Doing a Good Deed?

A great many people expect a reward when doing a good deed. First and foremost, there is a natural tendency to equate doing good deeds with receiving some form of reward—and often, that reward is assumed to be monetary. What is more, they argue that since money underpins contemporary society, earning it through commendable actions is both reasonable and practical.

On the contrary, the vast majority of people believe that doing a good deed should stem from personal conviction or moral motivation. Thus, the act itself is fulfilling, and external reward is of little significance. Numerous examples can be cited, but one suffices: Lei Feng lived a simple life dedicated to helping people from all walks of life without expecting any reward—and yet he is remembered as one of the most inspiring heroes of our time.

Generally speaking, it is my view that we should not expect a reward when doing a good deed. We do it for enjoyment, inner fulfillment, and spiritual growth—not for material gain.

Some prefer to dine at a fancy restaurant; some choose to take a vacation to an exotic destination for novel and thorough relaxation; others may pursue even more unconventional activities—such as bungee jumping, hiking, or cycling—to seek entirely new experiences, paying little attention to the Gala.

The Celebration of Western Festivals

Western festivals have gained ever-increasing popularity in China. A growing number of people are immersed in the thrilling atmosphere of the upcoming Christmas. In comparison with the Spring Festival, Christmas is given equally high status by some.

There are a variety of factors contributing to this trend. First, younger people are exposed to Western culture and lifestyles through learning English, and festivals are regarded as highlights of Western culture. For example, Valentine’s Day provides a vehicle for young adults to express their love. Second, economic development has increased Chinese people’s purchasing power. Businesses heavily target consumers, viewing foreign festivals as golden opportunities to make profits—so they actively promote the celebration of these festivals.

The necessity of celebrating foreign festivals is widely questioned. Some critics blame participants for weakening traditional values. Homegrown festivals play crucial roles in preserving Chinese traditional culture. However, their foreign counterparts are exerting increasing influence on people’s values and thinking. There is no doubt that we should prioritize Chinese traditional festivals.

Should the University Campus Be Open to Tourism?

Nowadays, many famous university campuses have become popular tourist attractions. TV and radio reports show that every year thousands of middle school students visit Tsinghua University, Peking University, and other renowned universities across China. Even in provinces far from the capital, local students travel to well-known universities within their own regions.

Is it beneficial or harmful to open university campuses to tourists? Opinions differ. On the one hand, some argue that such visits are beneficial: they help prospective students learn more about these institutions and motivate them to prepare thoroughly for admission. On the other hand, critics contend that public tourism harms universities—not only damaging the campus environment but also disturbing the academic atmosphere.

In my opinion, opening campuses to tourism is not advisable. A university campus is primarily a place for study and reflection. Increasing tourist traffic undermines its quiet, scholarly environment and erodes the spiritual atmosphere essential to learning.

Say No to Pirated Products

As is known to all, piracy has become an increasingly serious problem, hindering economic development. In many computers, we can find pirated Microsoft Windows software; in many DVD stores, pirated products are widely available.

Why does piracy persist? As far as I know, there are two main reasons. First, pirated products are much cheaper than legitimate ones. Take Windows as an example: the genuine software costs thousands of yuan, whereas a pirated copy costs only about five yuan. Second, many consumers fail to recognize the harms of purchasing pirated goods. These harms are significant. To begin with, producing pirated products amounts to theft—it is illegal. Moreover, if intellectual property rights are not adequately protected, companies will lose motivation to invest in innovation and high-quality products.

Although the problem is serious, effective measures can be taken. First, the government should enact stricter laws and enforce them rigorously to curb the production and distribution of pirated goods. Second, as responsible citizens and consumers, we must refuse to buy or use such products. Only through joint efforts—by authorities and individuals alike—can we effectively tackle this issue.

Next, we will go to the Ming Tombs, one of the best-preserved imperial tombs built for 13 emperors of the Ming Dynasty over 600 years ago. In the afternoon, we will tour the Summer Palace, the royal garden of China’s ancient emperors.

We are now on our way to the Great Wall. Dating back to the 7th century B.C., the Great Wall was originally constructed by separate states to defend against invasions from neighboring territories. Because of its long history and immense length, it is regarded as one of the Seven Wonders of the World and stands as a symbol of China’s highest wisdom and craftsmanship. From the top of the Wall, you can enjoy a magnificent view of rolling mountains, green trees, and blooming wildflowers. No wonder the saying goes, "He who has never been to the Great Wall is not a true man."

That concludes my introduction to the Great Wall. If you have any questions, please feel free to ask me at any time.

June 19, 2004

Dear Editor,

I am writing this letter to report some problems I recently encountered and to call for improvement in the service industry.

This weekend, I bought an English-Chinese dictionary at a bookstore near my home, attracted by its elaborately designed cover. However, when I got home and examined it carefully, I found that several pages were cracked and stained. Worse still, there were numerous misprints throughout the dictionary, seriously affecting my understanding.

Given such damage and printing errors, I returned to the bookstore to request a replacement. To my surprise, the staff refused my request rudely and even denied the dictionary’s poor quality.

It goes without saying that today’s fast-paced, market-oriented economy demands much higher standards from the service industry. Yet, to my regret, many businesses fail to meet these standards, and the competence and attitude of their staff need urgent improvement. Clearly, poor service quality not only deeply disappoints customers but also hinders the healthy development of our national economy. Therefore, I hope your newspaper will appeal to the service industry to place greater emphasis on service quality and customer satisfaction.

Thank you for your attention!

Sincerely yours,

It was about 9:00 a.m. on Saturday, June 15th. I was walking leisurely along the sidewalk outside my university on my way to visit a friend at another university when I heard a loud crash just ahead—at a T-junction about 10 meters away. Two taxis had collided head-on.

I rushed over and found both vehicles severely damaged: tires were deformed, and one door had been torn off and lay on the road. One driver was bleeding; the other was trapped inside his taxi. Several bystanders were trying to free the trapped driver, while another person was calling the traffic police. Traffic came to a standstill, with many cars backed up along the road.

From the skid marks on the road, it was clear that both taxis were traveling too fast. But speed alone was not the only cause. In my view, the drivers were overly eager to pick up more passengers and earn extra money. Moreover, neither showed due consideration for the other—both tried to go first. As a result, the accident was almost inevitable. We must remind all drivers that driving a little slower means staying a little safer. Caring for others’ lives is, in fact, caring for our own.

pastExams.essay:
Changes in Housing Ownership in China

Ownership of houses in China has changed greatly over the past decade. In the past, most houses were state-owned. But now, private houses are everywhere. As shown in the chart, in 1990, state-owned houses accounted for 75% of the total; this percentage dropped to 60% in 1995 and then sharply to 20% in 2000. Meanwhile, privately owned houses rose from 25% to 40%, and then to 80%.

There are mainly two reasons for this rapid change. First, the government has actively promoted policies supporting private housing development—policies that have proved vital to China’s economic growth. Second, with economic development, people’s living standards have improved, and more families aspire to own their own homes.

This shift has enabled many people to enjoy larger and better-quality living space. At the same time, however, it has also increased financial pressure, as individuals must earn more to afford home purchases.

It Pays to Be Honest

Although honesty is believed to be a virtue, there are still dishonest people in our society. For example, some businessmen sell fake products to their consumers; some students cheat in exams.

Dishonest people are short-sighted. Those who sell fake products may make money at first, but consumers will not buy their products anymore. As a result, they will lose their fortune—or even be sent to prison. By contrast, honest people gain a lot.

Those who always tell the truth or keep their promises not only earn others’ trust but also gain respect from other people. Such persons are sure to have many good friends. Because they are trustworthy and respectable, everyone is eager to make friends with them. Besides, it is easier for a person with a good record to get a good job. Generally speaking, every employer wants his or her employees to be honest. So we can say that anyone who is honest will be rewarded later.

In a word, honesty wins trust, respect, and honor. Therefore, it is important that we should be honest.

pastExams.essay:
How to Succeed in a Job Interview

Nowadays, in an ever-tighter job market, great importance has been attached to the interview by both employers and applicants. The interview, so to speak, has become indispensable for securing a satisfactory job. On the one hand, the interviewer can take advantage of the occasion to learn about the candidates—such as their work experience, education, and personalities—in order to select the right person for the company. On the other hand, the interviewee can use the opportunity to learn about the job, the salary, the working conditions, and many other aspects of the position he or she is interested in.

Therefore, the job interview is very important to a job seeker. But how can one succeed in it? First of all, the interviewee must pay attention to appearance. The first impression is always where we start: dress properly and neatly. Second, good manners are equally important. Don’t be too proud or too timid—just be courteous. Third, the interviewee must demonstrate aptitude and skills for the job, as well as knowledge of job-related areas. Be confident. Last but not least, the interviewee ought to be honest about his or her personal and academic background, for honesty is the best policy.

To sum up, the job interview is indeed important, but there is no need to be nervous. As long as the interviewee has the ability for the job, careful preparation—and a confident, honest performance—can ensure success.

Whether or not I take the test, I will make every effort to practice my spoken English during the remaining years of college.

pastExams.essay:
Reading Selectively or Extensively?

Some people think that when we read, we should read selectively. That is to say, we should choose books that interest us and ignore others. Reading selectively helps us concentrate our limited time and attention on those selected books.

Others believe we should read extensively—no matter what kind of book it is, we should browse it. We should read various kinds of books, whether or not we are interested in them. They maintain that extensive reading can broaden our horizons and help us acquire general knowledge across different fields.

In my opinion, both approaches have their respective merits in reading. However, the disadvantages of each method are also evident. If we read only the books we select or prefer, our knowledge framework may remain incomplete and rather limited. Conversely, if we read without selection, we may lack sufficient time and energy to specialize in any particular field. Therefore, a combination of both methods is more reasonable.

In our daily life, there are many occasions on which we should not hesitate to refuse when asked for help. For one thing, when a request is beyond our ability, we should give a direct reply: "No." For another, when what we are asked to do is unreasonable or even illegal, we should say "No" without hesitation.

However, this is not always the case in real life. Many people prefer to say "Yes" when they should say "No." Some are afraid of losing face, believing that refusal reflects their inability. Others fear offending acquaintances—such as friends or relatives.

My View on Fake Commodities

Nowadays, there are many fake commodities on the market—from daily necessities to expensive goods. They have caused serious harm to society.

First, fake commodities damage consumers’ interests. Moreover, they also harm legitimate businesses and manufacturers: deceived consumers may become reluctant to buy, leading to sluggish sales. Worst of all, some fake commodities—such as counterfeit medicines, faulty gas cylinders, and substandard electrical appliances—endanger people’s lives and undermine social security.

First, consumer protection laws must be strictly enforced to severely punish producers and sellers of fake goods. Third, they should be encouraged to safeguard their own rights and not be misled by false advertisements.

In a word, the whole society should pay close attention to the problem of fake commodities and launch a campaign against them. Only in this way can fake commodities possibly be eliminated from the market in the future.

First, they exaggerate the functions of the goods they advertise and mislead consumers. Second, some advertisements contain obscene content and bring about spiritual pollution. In conclusion, false advertisements must be eliminated from our society.

Perhaps when you went to some place far away from the city where you live and thought you knew nobody there, you were surprised to find one of your old classmates on the street! Both of you cried out, "What a small world!"

Why is the world getting smaller and smaller? For one thing, modern technology has created various means of transportation—and they are becoming increasingly accessible. Buses, trains, planes, and taxis operate in most cities around the world, carrying goods and passengers to and from every corner of the globe. For another thing, with the development of modern society, people are in contact with one another more frequently. Every day we interact with many people we did not know before. The more advanced a society is, the more contacts we make with others.

So we can conclude that as long as technology continues to advance, the world will grow smaller and smaller.

Therefore, to a great extent, one can take destiny into his own hands.

pastExams.essay:
To a Chinese, the task of learning English well is not easy. So I, like many other English learners, have met with difficulties in learning English during the past seven years. But I managed to overcome them and made much progress.

As to spelling, I never copied a new word again and again to remember it, but tried to find its relevance to the sound. In fact, as long as I can read the word out, I can write it out. As to the meaning, I rarely recited its Chinese translation but often put the word into a sentence to learn its meaning. Moreover, if you use a word quite often, its spelling and meaning will no longer be a problem. After all, we are learning English in order to use it.

I began to develop a feel for which sentences are "good English" and which are not.

Finally, I want to say that overcoming all these difficulties requires perseverance. In the past seven years, I spent at least an hour on English each day. I believe this is an important reason why I have been able to make progress in learning English.

Besides, permanent stations will be set up on the Moon or other planets so that scientists can conduct thorough studies of them. It is highly probable that extraterrestrial life will be discovered—or that planets suitable for human habitation will be found.

It is natural that we will encounter problems amid scientific and social progress. Therefore, we must be prepared to meet new challenges.

Meanwhile, grain consumption in people's diet consequently decreased.

From this analysis, we can conclude that our society is progressing and people are living a better life than ever before. We are now able to buy more delicious and nutritious food, resulting in improved health.

The bicycle is the most common means of transport in our country. There are several reasons for this. First, most people are not rich enough to buy a car. Since the bicycle is not expensive, it is affordable for the average Chinese family. Second, China has a large population and heavy traffic. The bicycle has the advantage of being small in size: a road that can accommodate only two cars may allow more than ten bicycles to travel side by side. Finally, people enjoy riding bicycles to school, to work, and on outings. It is pleasant, and the exercise is good for health.

The bicycle is popular in China and will remain so for a long time to come. Many changes must take place before cars become common in China. Therefore, in the foreseeable future, the bicycle will continue to be widely welcomed.

Disposable plastic bags were once widely used in China. When we went shopping at supermarkets and department stores, shop assistants often provided free plastic bags for our convenience. For a while, life without them seemed unimaginable to most of us.

However, disposable plastic bags cause severe damage to the environment. Customers usually throw them away after use, and because they are thin and difficult to decompose, these plastic products persist for hundreds of years. This poses a serious threat to our land and water resources.

Nowadays, the government has introduced regulations to limit the use of disposable plastic bags: they are no longer provided for free. In some stores, to raise public awareness of environmental protection, plastic bags are sold at a much higher price. As a result, people are changing their habits—paper bags and cloth bags, which had disappeared for a long time, are making a comeback in daily life. Indeed, by limiting their use, everyone contributes to improving the environment.

However, an increasing number of people have voiced different opinions about it, as more diverse lifestyles have emerged nowadays. Some prefer to dine at a fancy restaurant; some choose to take a vacation to an exotic destination for novel and thorough relaxation; others may pursue even more unconventional activities—such as bungee jumping, hiking, or cycling—to seek entirely new experiences, paying little attention to the Gala.

Should the University Campus Be Open to Tourism?

Nowadays, many famous university campuses have become popular tourist attractions. TV and radio reports show that every year thousands of middle school students visit Tsinghua University, Peking University, and other renowned universities across China. Even in provinces far from the capital, local students travel to well-known universities within their own regions.

Is it beneficial or harmful to open university campuses to tourists? Opinions differ. On the one hand, some argue that such visits are beneficial: they help prospective students learn more about these institutions and motivate them to prepare thoroughly for admission. On the other hand, critics contend that public tourism harms universities—not only damaging the campus environment but also disturbing the academic atmosphere.

In my opinion, opening campuses to tourism is not advisable. A university campus is primarily a place for study and reflection. Increasing tourist traffic undermines its quiet, scholarly environment and erodes the spiritual atmosphere essential to learning.

No wonder the saying goes, "He who has never been to the Great Wall is not a true man."

That concludes my introduction to the Great Wall. If you have any questions, please feel free to ask me at any time.

An Eye-Witness Account of a Traffic Accident

My name is Liming, and I am a college student. A week ago, I witnessed a traffic accident that remains vivid in my memory.

It was about 9:00 a.m. on Saturday, June 15th. I was walking leisurely along the sidewalk outside my university on my way to visit a friend at another university when I heard a loud crash just ahead—at a T-junction about 10 meters away. Two taxis had collided head-on.

I rushed over and found both vehicles severely damaged: tires were deformed, and one door had been torn off and lay on the road. One driver was bleeding; the other was trapped inside his taxi. Several bystanders were trying to free the trapped driver, while another person was calling the traffic police. Traffic came to a standstill, with many cars backed up along the road.

From the skid marks on the road, it was clear that both taxis were traveling too fast. But speed alone was not the only cause. In my view, the drivers were overly eager to pick up more passengers and earn extra money. Moreover, neither showed due consideration for the other—both tried to go first. As a result, the accident was almost inevitable. We must remind all drivers that driving a little slower means staying a little safer. Caring for others’ lives is, in fact, caring for our own.

It Pays to Be Honest

Although honesty is believed to be a virtue, there are still dishonest people in our society. For example, some businessmen sell fake products to their consumers; some students cheat in exams.

Dishonest people are short-sighted. Those who sell fake products may make money at first, but consumers will not buy their products anymore. As a result, they will lose their fortune—or even be sent to prison. By contrast, honest people gain a lot.

Those who always tell the truth or keep their promises not only earn others’ trust but also gain respect from other people. Such persons are sure to have many good friends. Because they are trustworthy and respectable, everyone is eager to make friends with them. Besides, it is easier for a person with a good record to get a good job. Generally speaking, every employer wants his or her employees to be honest. So we can say that anyone who is honest will be rewarded later.

In a word, honesty wins trust, respect, and honor. Therefore, it is important that we should be honest.

Should Students Go Abroad for Study at an Early Age?

Every year, tens of thousands of teenagers go abroad to study in pursuit of a brighter future. The number of such students is steadily increasing, raising widespread concern. People are divided on whether students should study abroad at an early age.

In my opinion, if feasible, young students should consider studying abroad early. Firstly, it is widely accepted that the younger one is, the more quickly and effectively one can acquire a foreign language. Students living abroad naturally gain abundant opportunities to practice and master the target language. Secondly, as we know, competition in China’s national college entrance examination (the Gaokao) is extremely fierce, leaving many students unable to pursue higher education domestically. Studying abroad offers an alternative pathway for them to fulfill their academic potential. Thirdly, contrary to the popular notion that young overseas students lead carefree lives, their experience is often full of challenges. They learn to live independently and develop greater appreciation for what they have—especially since many were previously overindulged by parents and grandparents at home.

In conclusion, studying abroad at an early age brings significant benefits. On the one hand, students enhance their linguistic competence, academic skills, and psychological resilience. On the other hand, society also benefits when these well-trained talents return home to contribute to national development.

Psychology plays an important role in our daily life. If you possess a healthy psychological state, you will have confidence to overcome many difficulties. On the contrary, poor mental health may leave you feeling sad and frustrated throughout your life. Therefore, maintaining psychological well-being is essential.

There are at least three ways to maintain a healthy psychology. First, learn to regulate your emotions when facing chaos—for example, during depression or under stress. Third, cultivate self-discipline, which helps you remain rational and composed even when you are on the verge of losing control.

As far as I am concerned, treating everyone around you with kindness and staying calm when angry are important ways to foster psychological well-being.

Besides reading in my spare time, I played table tennis for fun and made enormous progress.

I will never forget those special days when I took my first step in college.

For a college student, the advantages of having roommates generally outweigh the disadvantages. Those who object to having roommates claim that living with several people gives rise to unpleasantness because everyone has his or her own habits and preferences. They also argue that shared living usually means a lack of privacy.

Although these arguments sound reasonable at first glance, they are not fully supported by careful consideration. When you and your roommates disagree or face conflicts, it is an excellent opportunity to learn how to manage interpersonal relationships. Solving everyday problems in the dorm—such as sharing chores or respecting quiet hours—enriches your social experience, helps you understand others’ feelings, and fosters empathy and consideration.

Moreover, dormitory life offers an invaluable chance for cooperation and participation in lively group activities. Planning a party alone may be dull and difficult; with your roommates’ help, however, it becomes enjoyable and manageable. You can brainstorm ideas together, divide tasks, and even start a music club or study group. Such experiences build teamwork skills and lifelong friendships.

In conclusion, sharing a dormitory is a precious opportunity for college students. It is one of the best ways to learn cooperation, deepen understanding of others, and gain early insight into social life.

essays.body:
Today's Luxuries Are Tomorrow's Necessities

By "luxury", we mean "a pleasant and often expensive thing that is not necessary". From a historical point of view, most things that were luxuries when first invented later became necessities. When the electric bulb was first invented in the U.S., it was such a luxury that only government bodies could afford it. Nowadays, however, it is found in every part of the world. The same is true of the telephone, television, and many other inventions that were once considered luxuries.

Anything, no matter how luxurious it may seem, tends to become a necessity once it is widely adopted. This holds true for many present-day luxuries, including mobile phones, cars, and computers. It is widely acknowledged that the purpose of scientific development is to make life easier for humanity—not just for a privileged few. Therefore, after a new invention appears, the priority is to disseminate it widely so as to benefit as many people as possible. During this process, the item gradually loses its luxurious status until it eventually becomes a necessity. This reflects an objective social trend.

With the rapid advancement of science and technology, the time it takes for an innovation to evolve from luxury to necessity is greatly shortened. Many things once thought unimaginable are now invented—and quickly become accessible to ordinary people.

On Mobile Phones

Mobile phones are gaining increasing popularity among people from all walks of life in modern society. They are commonly used by a wide range of people—from students on campus to professional workers who have already established their careers. In fact, mobile phones have gradually become an integral part of our daily lives.

Despite their widespread popularity, we should not overlook the fact that their excessive or improper use can lead to numerous problems. First, the radiation emitted by mobile phones may cause some harm to human health. More importantly, their signals can interfere with sensitive electronic equipment—especially in hospitals or at airports—posing a potential threat to safety and normal operations. Besides, overreliance on mobile phones may disrupt our daily routines and interpersonal communication.

Since it is unrealistic to abandon mobile phones altogether due to their negative effects, the only sensible solution is to use them responsibly. To begin with, we should limit usage time—using phones only when necessary. In addition, the public should be better informed about the associated risks, enabling more conscious and disciplined usage.

Is Score Important?

Too much emphasis is placed on test scores, which is one of the most obvious features of today's education. On the one hand, scores have become the most important criterion for college enrollment. On the other hand, they are also among the crucial factors in job assignments and employment competitions.

Overemphasizing test scores brings many negative effects on students' learning as well as on teachers' teaching. Firstly, students tend to focus more on strategies for achieving high scores than on developing their overall capabilities. Secondly, teachers may inflate grades, as their performance is often judged primarily by students’ scores. Thirdly, some students who excel in exams prove less competent in real-world tasks.

Personally, I believe test scores can reflect a student’s academic performance to some extent, but they cannot represent overall ability. Excessive focus on scores actually undermines the fundamental goals of education.

How to Really Interest Customers

Various businessmen provide discounts in order to attract more customers. Low prices are quite appealing to those who are short of money or want to save money. In fact, this strategy has brought in a great number of customers for businessmen over the past decades.

However, this strategy has been losing its effect in recent years. Price no longer functions as a decisive factor in most people’s purchasing decisions. They are increasingly aware of the importance of product quality.

In my opinion, there are two main ways to really attract customers. On the one hand, businessmen must make full efforts to improve the quality of their products. On the other hand, good after-sales service must be provided to meet customers’ needs. Only by doing so can businessmen truly attract more and more customers.
